newsitem.title: POLAND: Netia to invest $200 million in Poland.
newsitem.headline: Netia to invest $200 million in Poland.

text.p: Local telephone operator Netia Telekom SA, a Polish-international consortium, plans to invest $200 million by the end of the year to boost its network, an official of the firm's board said on Wednesday.
"Our investment plan is $200 million," the board's deputy head Jan Guz told Reuters over the telephone.

He said Netia, in which the Swedish firm Telia AB holds 25 percent and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development has 10 percent, planned to increase the number of customers to 200,000 in 1997 from the current 40,000.
The investment will be financed from a $180 million loan from the EBRD, Chase Investment Bank, Bank Handlowy and from the company's own resources, Guz said.
Netia now operates only local telephone links because the state-owned firm TPSA enjoys a monopoly on more lucrative inter-city and long-distance connections.

Netia's network currently covers 22 percent of Poland's area and the company wants to expand its service to 40 percent of the area, if the telecommunications ministry grants it operation licences. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
